source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Recognize an infusion-related vancomycin reaction associated with rapid administration, including upper-body flushing and pruritus.","B":"Recognize definite IgE-mediated anaphylaxis solely from the flushing pattern even though the airway and blood pressure remain stable.","C":"Interpret the flushing as evidence of inadequate vancomycin exposure and increase the infusion because this reaction indicates underdosing.","D":"Interpret the rash as unrelated to vancomycin because rapid infusion is not associated with flushing or pruritic skin findings."}}
source_row.rationale: Current vancomycin labeling describes infusion-related events during or soon after rapid infusion, including flushing of the upper body, pruritus, urticaria, and sometimes hypotension or respiratory findings. Option A is correct because the timing and stable airway and blood pressure fit an infusion-related reaction. Option B overcalls definite IgE-mediated anaphylaxis from flushing alone. Option C incorrectly interprets the reaction as underdosing. Option D contradicts the known infusion-related adverse-reaction profile.
source_row.source_detail: DailyMed Vancomycin Hydrochloride for Injection — Warnings and Precautions/Adverse Reactions, Infusion Reactions: rapid IV administration may produce upper-body flushing, pruritus, urticaria, hypotension, wheezing/dyspnea, and chest/back muscle spasm; infusion-rate reduction lowers risk. Current FDA vancomycin hydrochloride injection labeling at cited DailyMed set ID; live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: medication routes, administration, reversal, adverse effects/interactions, withdrawal, monitoring and client teaching. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

source_row.stem: A client develops upper-body flushing and pruritus during a rapid vancomycin infusion while blood pressure and airway remain stable. What is the best interpretation?
